issues.description: The problem statement uses informal attribute names 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' (problem_statement.md) which do not match the attribute identifiers shown in the UML and used in the solution and expected template implementation ('numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'). This naming inconsistency in the specification can confuse students about the exact attribute names they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent across the problem statement and UML. Update the prose in problem_statement.md to use the exact attribute identifiers shown in the UML and implemented in the solution (e.g. 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'), or explicitly note the alternate informal synonyms to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement's task text refers to attributes named 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents', while the UML diagram and the solution implementation use the names 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This naming mismatch for the same conceptual attributes (counts of students) can confuse students when adding fields and implementing the constructor (order and names expected by tests/UML).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent across artifacts. Update the problem statement task text to use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (matching the UML and solution) or explicitly note that 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' refer to the same counts and should be declared as 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' in code.
